author.name: Susan B. Anthony
author.heading: About Susan B. Anthony
author.bio: Susan B. Anthony organized for the abolition of slavery and for women's voting rights. Her partnership with Elizabeth Cady Stanton joined public speaking, lobbying and publishing in a long campaign for equality.

cite.sourceCitation: Anthony, Susan B. “Social Purity.” In Ida Husted Harper, The Life and Work of Susan B. Anthony, vol. II, 1004–1012, at 1008. Indianapolis and Kansas City: Bowen-Merrill, 1898.
cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘Independence is happiness’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: In the speech, Anthony moves from the need for women in paid work and the professions to a literary example of a dependent man discovering freedom. The surrounding passage ↗ makes independence a practical condition of happiness, not simply a pleasant mood.
